# x86_semantics.py cases where Rosetta and an x86 CPU differ: what it left (docs/macos/integer-data/silicon_overrides.py writes this file). One corpus line per family run on the x86 CPU, an AMD EPYC 9V74 (raven-macos-bench run 44522713416, assembled with clang as here; dump sha256 03387cc62d468ee5703fa26b4435465680cf096261e0e45c20b81e97adfeaa95; the random family alone first in run 44522174773). The tests refuse the file when a family's cases or Rosetta's results change. The random family's one difference, the RAX a 32-bit lock cmpxchg leaves, was first found on an AMD EPYC 9V45 (run 44411803673). In the multiply and divide families the EPYC agrees with Rosetta in every register and defined flag; they differ only in flags x86 leaves undefined (1039 and 1231 cases), which the tests do not compare.
corpus	divide	cases=1303	generated=d44ddee864ebb516	rosetta=67812a74a69526f7
corpus	multiply	cases=1120	generated=2153868388b91462	rosetta=8329c158c8aa4e17
corpus	random	cases=10000	generated=29504b896eccb080	rosetta=70e1f67988c68548
8316	lea r12, [r8 + 2*rbx + -9550]; cmpxchg qword ptr [r15 + 0], r14; lock cmpxchg dword ptr [r15 + 0], r14d; not r9d	rosetta=bef3e01ee61d7fc6	r0=7ca1c6eb10355a7f
